models.structure: 231 disjoint one-hot equality groups of 231 binaries each (53,361 members, RHS 1), 231 y binaries with sum y = 13, one continuous z >= 0, 53,361 link rows x - y <= 0, 53,130 rows d_ij*x_ij - z <= 0 with exact positive rational d, 231 identical rows -z <= 0, 231 y-links per y; every group has exactly one zero-distance member.

edit_semantics: Row-set replacement with strengthening - not a bound change and not a pure deletion. Target = source minus 53,130 rows d_ij*x_ij - z <= 0 minus the 231 identical rows -z <= 0, plus 231 rows sum_j d_ij*x_ij - z <= 0 (named AGG_<one-hot row>). The 231 -z<=0 rows are a true deletion (implied by the bound z >= 0); the 53,130 replaced rows are subsumed by the aggregate for x >= 0, d >= 0, so the relaxed set shrinks strictly (a source-LP-feasible fractional point violates all 231 aggregates). The tightened object is therefore a NEW ROW whose LHS is the group weighted sum, not a tightened variable bound. Columns, bounds, integrality, RHS, objective are numerically unchanged; only the model NAME changes cosmetically. Counts: -53,130 rows (49.68%) and -53,130 nonzeros (19.91%).
claims: Claim 0 {reverse:false, input_integers:true, output_integers:true, objective:'Equal', inverse:1}: forward integer inclusion; all 53,824 target rows are checked - 231 aggregates derived per group by exhaustive integer Cases, 53,593 retained rows cited directly; projection is the identity on all 53,593 coordinates.

Claim 1 {reverse:true, input/output_integers:true, inverse:0}: reverse integer inclusion; the 53,361 deleted rows are re-derived - 53,130 from the aggregate plus sibling nonnegativity (split_upper), 231 from {VarLower:z} - while retained rows are cited.
Claim 2 {reverse:true, input/output_integers:false, inverse:None}: target LP inclusion into the source LP; the request binds the strictness point to this index ({"Strictness":{"inclusion_claim":2}}).

Point 0: 53,593 exact rational values (x = 1/231 on all 53,361 one-hot members, y = 13/231 on the 231 y variables, z = 6080563905636779/28875000000000); every source row and bound passes and all 231 aggregate rows are violated.

Contract: complete original-coordinate mixed-integer feasible-set equality plus exact objective equality plus reciprocal full identity inverses (53,593 'Exact' obligations each way), with strict LP strengthening certified by point 0; no optimum restriction or objective monotonicity assumed.
proof_encoding: 'RPA 3' header plus a single JSON line of 185,396,387 B: {claims:[3], blocks:[3 nested blocks], points:[1]}; measured top-level offsets: claims+identity projections 0-2,184,597, forward block 2,184,597-125,873,442, reverse-integer block -156,084,729, reverse-LP block -184,967,316.

Forward block (231 groups): a balanced depth-8 tree of Cases{kind:'Le', expression:(subtree weighted sum minus z), split:(integer subset sum), integer:(derived Int fact), left/right:{steps, end:{Witness}}}; leaves cite the actual individual RowUpper row, or {VarLower:z} for the zero-distance member.

Per Cases branch: EqPair converts the branch assumption into the sibling's zero-sum equality, a Lin step derives the checked zero-sibling weighted contribution (weighted_zero), and the final Lin combines the selected subtree bound with that contribution into the aggregate expression.

Reverse block: a tree of nonnegativity facts -w_j*x_j <= 0 (Lin over VarLower), then split_upper Lin steps that add the sibling nonnegativity to the aggregate bound to recover each individual row; the 231 -z<=0 rows are discharged by {VarLower:z}.

Return per claim: map = 53,593 identity expressions, checks = VarLower/VarUpper (+VarInt inside integral claims) per variable, one ref per output row, one 'Exact' for objective equality plus 53,593 'Exact' inverse coordinates; obligations 321,788 / 374,918 / 267,733.

friction: The domain agent's single failing tool call was its own Python SyntaxError (unmatched ')', digest 'File "<cell>", line 32'); no kernel rejection was ever exercised during the reformulation run.

The kernel has no aggregation rule, so 53,130 Cases records and 964,439 obligations were composed by hand, including every derived precondition (Int fact, nonnegativity, complement, zero-sibling lemma).
Each of the 5 negative checks rewrites the entire 185 MB RPA text and re-assembles plus re-verifies (tools/prepare_test34.py:113), because there is no cheaper way to re-verify one claim.

Recorded INVALID receipts carry only a message (for example 'INVALID obligation mismatch: expected Le; obligation 160785') with no group or member attribution, although the API now adds code and location.
The identity projection/inverse is written out in full - 53,593 pairs in request.json (2,184,640 B, essentially the whole file) and again in the claims section of every RPA (first 2,184,597 B).
